source: She told me he accosted her in her private chambers! In her own bed. Mad as a horse in heat!
Heated as a stag in rut, as a hound in—
I get the point, Polonius.
Excellent. That's all I wanted to impart.
Of course I've given word to Ophelia to rebuke him, disregarding whatever dalliance they once had.
As well we know they did, once.
I saw him departing my daughter's room just a few minutes ago.
She wouldn't tell me anything about it, either.
But if all of this is true, then Hamlet is in a worse state than even I anticipated.
Are you sure he wasn't invited in?
Not a chance!—That is, no offense to young Hamlet, of course.
My lady, what my father says is true. I didn't invite Hamlet into my chambers.
And he seemed to be unusually disturbed.
Oh, my. My apologies, then, Ophelia.
When he returned from Wittenberg, I thought... well.
Now, now. None of that talk here, love.
There may be more to this than mere lovesickness.
What do you mean by that?
You and I should meet to discuss this further, privately. Perhaps tomorrow. In the meantime, Lady Ophelia, I urge you to stay away from Hamlet.
Of course, my lord.
I believe convening the war council is our highest priority at the moment.
I'll withhold my less pressing security concerns until we've had the opportunity to meet.
But you should also know, my lord, I've taken Lady Brit into custody.
Just this morning, Lady Ophelia informed me of some suspicious behavior, and I had my men investigate Lady Brit's chambers.
Brit? Truly?
Lord Fortinbras will stop at nothing to prize apart our court. Even turning good, strong Danish families against us.
I fear this is a sign of far graver things to come.
Isn't it possible that this is all in error, Bernardo? Being mistaken here would be a grave insult to the Brockenhuus family.
Unlikely, my lady. The connection was clear once we found quite a lot of documentation in her chambers.
I... I see. Then what should come of this?
While the news is certainly distressing, let us keep it within Elsinore for now.
As new information presents itself, we shall be compelled to do more. Let us stay our hands until then. Those are my wishes.
I-if you're certain that's the correct course of action, my King, then so be it.
That is all. You may adjourn.
I turn to the court with a more pressing matter.
My lord, I believe the possibility exists that someone disloyal to Denmark exists within this court, and they may wish to do you harm.
And yet perhaps it is no more than a hunch.
I have good reason to believe this threat is real.
Would you stake a life on it?
Let him continue, Polonius.
You mean a spy?
Indeed. A spy amongst us. I have good reason to believe this threat is real. It may even be from outside Denmark.
For example, though I welcome Fortinbras' request to cross our lands on his way to attack Poland, we cannot ignore that he recently threatened to wage war on us.
A missing keyring, coded messages found just outside the castle—these are the signs of subterfuge. We have dealt with it before.
I believe the threat is not simply outside Elsinore's walls, but within them as well.
Hrm. Come to think of it, I found certain personal items of mine disturbed last night, after my door was bolted for the evening.
If true, this is deeply worrying. We must be dilligent.
However, as we have no culprit in hand, I cannot yet take this threat seriously.
Bernardo, I task you with speaking to all those who might have further information.
Yes, my lord.
I am already investigating some compelling leads.
I believe the investigation has merit.
My lord, I've taken Lady Brit into custody.
I-If you're certain that's the correct course of action, my King, then so be it.
What are you reading, my Prince?
Nothing. Just words. Words, words, words.
Certainly one presumes so, unless you have become illiterate! But do tell me, words about what?
Meaningless drivel. This author thinks old men have wrinkled faces and grey beards. What does he know? About anything?
He says that they prattle on and on and on, thinking they are wise when really they have no wisdom at all.
And weak thighs, at that. I find the notion odd, since old men could be as young as I if they only walked backwards like crabs.
(The boy's insane. Or is he simply mocking me? Though this be madness, yet there is method in it.)
What did you say?
Nothing, my Prince. I should take my leave.
Ah, good. There is nothing I'd rather you take. Except, perhaps, my life.
What's happening to me...?
Rosie? Guilda? What... what in Hell are you both doing here?
Coming to visit you, of course!
We were on our way to stuff our faces at the German court—
—To pay our respects, she means—
Right, right. And we thought we'd pay you a visit, too.
You came... purely to see me?
Of course! So what's got you down, old friend?
I mean, aside from your father dying in that awful snake incident... bitten in the garden, was it?
Guilda, you're being obscene.
Who knew Danish snakes were such a prolific threat?
Honestly!—Hamlet, we truly are sorry to hear about your father's passing. Really.
It's... it's all right. Listen. You're not being straight with me. Why are you both here?
Did you really come of your own accord?
What? Rosie, that's not true. What about that letter from his uncle—
I see.
My uncle sent you.
I knew it. The dog... he's got even you two watching me now.
No. Believe us, Hamlet, we came only to pay our respects. Not for anything nefarious.
Your new father seems worried about you!
Ah, Hamlet, you know, business aside, that odd little performer man you like so much is coming to Denmark. We saw him coming up the road.
Peter Quince? Really?
Peter Quince? Yes, so I've learned.
(So they are coming after all. Ophelia was right...)
Er, Hamlet? You're muttering?
Nothing, nothing. What was it you were saying?
It's been years since we last saw Quince perform, hasn't it?
A show's already been arranged for the whole court tomorrow night!
Yes. That sounds... more wonderful than anything that's happened lately.
When I was younger, I believe he often allowed me to provide input on his performance.
Sometimes he'd even let me contribute to the script.
Sounds delightful. And distracting from all the darkness lately!
Yes. Distracting.
The Playmaster Peter Quince has already arrived in Elsinore. He should be nearby.
...Peter Quince, right.
Well, my friends, I think you may have been of use to me after all.
I'll see you both at the performance.
I shall go to see him.
Maybe it'll help to... distract me from less savory matters.
I've already been to see him, in fact.
I'll see you both at the performance tomorrow night.
Quince, my good man! Welcome to Elsinore!
My pleasure. It is truly a treat to return.
I think we could use some drama right now. Some comedy or tragedy. Perhaps one, then the other.
Though a tragedy better fits the mood of the castle, I think.
Hee hee hee... I can more than provide, my dear Prince.
I've heard the performance is to start tomorrow night?
Indeed, my lord. Why, I'm already hard at work on the script!
Wait. Are you already planning a performance here in Elsinore?
Indeed, my lord. For tomorrow night. Why, I'm already hard at work on the script!
You mean... you haven't written it yet?
Oh, no. I'm an improvisational artist, you see. My performances adapt to the local conversation at hand.
So much more topical that way. You understand, I'm sure.
How interesting. I have some ideas, but no stroke of genius quite yet. Let me think on it a while.
We'll speak more tomorrow.
Of course, my lord. I'll be waiting.
My good man Quince.
Lord Hamlet! Good morning.
If I have your permission, Quince, I have some suggestions for what play to perform tonight.
Something... appropriately sobering. Something... reflective.
And if you wouldn't mind, I'd like to add a line or two myself.
I'm told I'm quite handy with a goosequill.
But of course, my lord. I would not dream of denying you a voice.
And I do so love a guest writer. What have you brought me?
Here. The script.
Hmm. 'The Murder of Gonzago?' Fascinating. Yes, I think we can work with this.
But won't your dear uncle the King be upset?
I certainly hope so.
Speak the speech, I pray you, trippingly on the tongue.
I will, sir!
Tell me, did you learn anything about the origins of Hamlet's insanity?
No. It's most confusing, my lord.
Certainly unlike him!
Yes, most unlike him, certainly!
Hmmm. Maybe Polonius had more luck.
By the way, Hamlet was cheered to hear the Playmaster Quince is returning.
Yes, I thought inviting him might lift Hamlet's spirits just a little.
We can stand to give up the Great Hall for just an evening, I think.
Then perhaps you'll be cheered to know that Hamlet's rather keen on the idea.
So I've heard, but I didn't dare to believe it. How wonderful!
Wonderful! Hamlet? Really? You're certain?
Hamlet's father always liked to see Quince perform. I think he found the man's work relatable. I'm glad to see my son does, too.
Isn't that right, my love?
Yes. Right.
All recent events have made it clear Hamlet is dangerous and must be dealt with.
Perhaps it's time we fulfilled his request to be sent away.
Back to university at Wittenberg, you mean?
Wittenberg? No, no. The prince deserves to see new sights, don't you think?
I was thinking England. Something like... assisting on a 'diplomatic' endeavor. On behalf of the Danish throne, that is.
My lord, I recommend a bit of targeted spying, first.
Maybe we can learn something that will help us.
Very well, Polonius. If that is what you think best.
I shall give you another chance to prove yourself. Let us hope you learn something of use.
Perhaps if we catch him and my daughter together, I can finally show my theories are justified!
Hmmm. Yes.
To be or not to be...
That is the question.
Whether it's nobler to try and suffer through the pain...
Or turn our backs to all of it and welcome the inevitable embrace of death a little earlier.
To die—to sleep no more—And by sleeping, I mean to end the heartache, the thousand little pains I have to bear.
